s: Background job processor that dequeues tasks and executes long-running or deferred work off the critical request path.
w: Consumers poll message queues (SQS, RabbitMQ, Kafka) or claim tasks from a job table. Each worker pulls a message, executes the job (email send, image resize, report build), and acks on success or nacks on failure for retry. Concurrency is controlled by prefetch limits or process pools. Horizontal scaling means adding more consumer instances; the queue absorbs bursts.
use: Asynchronous tasks: email sending, PDF generation, image transcoding
Retry-heavy integrations with flaky third-party APIs
Batch data processing: nightly aggregation, CSV export, deduplication
Rate-limited API calls to external services (spaced request patterns)
avoid: Request-path work needing sub-second response (requesters block waiting)
Tasks requiring user-facing real-time feedback without a polling/webhook mechanism
Lightweight glue that a serverless function handles cheaper

props.concurrency: Number of parallel jobs per worker instance
props.retry_policy: Max retries, backoff strategy, dead-letter routing

pat.d: Repeatedly failing jobs park in DLQ for manual inspection and replay.
Multiple workers dequeue from same queue distributing load automatically.

pits: Poison messages looping forever - implement max retries with DLQ escalation
Memory leaks from accumulated job objects in long-lived workers - periodic restarts or leak profiling
Visibility timeout expiring before slow job finishes - extend heartbeat or split large jobs
tips: Idempotency is non-negotiable: duplicate deliveries are guaranteed eventually at scale
Queue depth as a scaling signal: sustained backlog means add consumers, transient spikes are fine
